name: Hoshiyar Puri
why_it_matters: Opened 1937 on Upper Road, opposite Gaurakhnath Mandir, ~5 minutes from Har Ki Pauri. The Haridwar pilgrim's Punjabi-Sindhi canteen — same family, two adjacent buildings, no menu deviation in nearly nine decades. The aloo-poori-kheer combo is what regulars order before they sit down.
insider_tip: Skip the lunch rush (12:30-2:30) — pilgrim buses arrive in waves. Mid-morning (9:30-11) is when the kheer is freshest and you'll get a table on the first floor.
signature_address: Upper Road, opposite Gaurakhnath Mandir, near Mansa Devi stairway, Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar 249401

name: Mathura Walo Ki Pracheen Dukan
why_it_matters: Multi-generation sweet house in Moti Bazaar near Thanda Kuan — a TripAdvisor top-5 Haridwar listing on traveller volume alone. The peda comes from the Mathura tradition that gave the shop its name; everything else (jalebi, kachori, kaddu sabzi) is fried in pure desi ghee.
insider_tip: Seating is six-seven tables for the whole shop — expect a 20-30 minute wait at peak. Order the puri with kaddu (pumpkin) sabzi, not the chole; the kaddu is the dish locals come back for.
signature_address: Near Thanda Kuan, Moti Bazaar, Bara Bazar, Haridwar 249401

name: Mohan Ji Puri Wale
why_it_matters: Two outlets on Har Ki Pauri Marg — a stand-up street counter near the police station and a sit-down annexe behind it. The post-aarti breakfast destination for pilgrims; puris come out of the oil in batches every two minutes.
insider_tip: The street counter is faster but you'll eat standing. Walk 30 seconds further to the dine-in shop for the same food on a leaf plate with a chair — same kitchen, no queue.
signature_address: Har Ki Pauri Marg, near police station, Haridwar 249401

name: Pandit Ji Poori Wale
why_it_matters: Sit-down poori shop on Hanuman Ghat Road — quieter than the Har Ki Pauri counters, traditional banana-leaf service, the four-poori thali (gravy sabzi + dry sabzi + sweetish chutney) is the standard order. TripAdvisor 4.6 from a small but consistent review base.
insider_tip: Walk five minutes upstream from Har Ki Pauri towards Hanuman Ghat — most pilgrims don't, which is exactly why the queue here is shorter than Mohan Ji Puri Wale's.
signature_address: Hanuman Ghat Road, near Kasha Ghat, Haridwar 249401

name: Aahar Restaurant
why_it_matters: Railway Road sit-down — the bookmarked option for pilgrims arriving by train who want a hot thali within ten minutes of leaving the platform. Punjabi-South-Indian mix; not as old as Hoshiyar Puri but reliably the cleanest mid-range table inside a 500m radius of the station.
insider_tip: If you're catching an evening train, eat here at 5-6pm rather than the platform stalls — same price for proper food, and the kitchen plates a thali in 8 minutes flat.
signature_address: Railway Road, near Haridwar Junction, Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar 249401

name: Bara Bazar Aloo Tikki Stalls
why_it_matters: The Bara Bazar lane between Subhash Ghat and the railway has the city's densest cluster of tikki and gol-gappa carts — a moving line of vendors rather than one fixed institution. This is the late-evening chaat circuit pilgrims walk after the aarti.
insider_tip: Pick stalls with the longest local queue, not the ones angled toward tourists. Watch for fresh tamarind chutney being ladled from a steel container — the orange sweet syrup-only versions are tourist short-cuts.
signature_address: Bara Bazar lanes between Subhash Ghat and Railway Road, Haridwar 249401
